question: Should Crabline unconditionally reject correctly signed Discord interactions when their signed timestamp differs from the host clock by more than five minutes, despite Discord not documenting that cutoff?
rationale: The rule strengthens replay resistance but adds an undocumented fail-closed compatibility requirement that can disable all Discord interactions on a clock-drifted host.

options.title: Verify and keep five minutes
options.body: Retain the hardening after confirming it against a live Discord interaction flow and make clock-skew failures diagnosable.

options.title: Make freshness opt-in
options.body: Preserve signature-only compatibility by default and expose strict timestamp enforcement as an explicit policy setting.

options.title: Keep signature-only behavior
options.body: Drop the freshness rejection and continue matching Discord's documented validation procedure exactly.

recommendation.title: Verify and keep five minutes
recommendation.body: Retain the hardening after confirming it against a live Discord interaction flow and make clock-skew failures diagnosable.
